findings.title: Slots on a date-override day skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body:
When the slot's day has a date override and the slot passes the range checks, `checkIfIsAvailable` hits `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`. That returns before `busy.every(...)` runs.

On any day with a date override, the user's existing Cal bookings and connected-calendar busy times are therefore ignored. All users of a non-team event count as fixed hosts, so this affects personal event types too, not only round-robin. Invitees can book slots that overlap existing bookings or calendar events.

Only the working-hours check should be skipped when an override exists. The busy check must still run.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects every slot when a user has more than one working-hours entry for a day
findings.body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns true, and the slot is rejected, if the slot falls outside ANY working-hours entry that includes the slot's UTC weekday. It should only reject when the slot is inside none of them.

`getWorkingHours` splits ranges that cross UTC midnight into two entries with shifted `days`. Example: a PST user working Mon–Fri 9–17 gets {days 1–5, 1020–1439} and {days 2–6, 0–60}.
- A Tuesday 18:00Z slot fits the first entry but is outside the second, so it is rejected.
- A Tuesday 00:30Z slot is rejected by the first entry.

Result: organizers in most western-hemisphere timezones lose almost all Tue–Fri availability. Users with split schedules (e.g. 9–12 and 13–17 on the same day) lose all slots on those days.

The logic should accept a slot that fits within at least one applicable entry.

findings.title: Slot end used for the working-hours check is computed from the slot start
findings.body:
`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. The intended `end > workingHour.endTime` check therefore only tests the slot's start.

A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end is accepted. For example, a 60-minute event at 17:30 with working hours ending at 18:00 passes. This should use `slotEndTime`, taking care with slots that end exactly at midnight.

findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges on the same day reject all slots
findings.body:
`dateOverrides.find` returns true, and the slot is marked unavailable, as soon as ANY override on the slot's day doesn't contain the slot.

Date overrides support several time ranges per day (e.g. 9–10 and 14–15). A slot in the first range is outside the second, and vice versa, so every slot on that day is rejected for the fixed host. The check should reject only when the slot is outside ALL override ranges for that day.

findings.title: Override range check accepts slots that only partially overlap the override
Dayjs objects compared with `===`, so the 'unavailable all day' branch never runs
findings.body:
`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references, so it is always false. Overrides that mark a day unavailable (start == end) never take this early-reject path.

The later checks miss a slot starting exactly at the override instant (midnight in the organizer's zone), because `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` is false for equal times. Since `dateOverrideExist` is then true, the function returns true and also skips the busy check. A slot at midnight on a day the host marked unavailable can therefore be offered. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

findings.title: Override day is matched by UTC calendar day instead of the organizer's local day, and formatted in server-local time
findings.body:
The code checks whether the slot is on the override's day by comparing the UTC date of the override's real start instant with the slot's UTC date. A date override covers a calendar day in the organizer's timezone.

Example: a PST organizer sets an override for day D 16:00–20:00, i.e. D+1 00:00Z–04:00Z. The real start falls on UTC day D+1.
- Slots during the organizer's day D (e.g. D 17:00Z = 09:00 PST) don't match, so normal working hours apply and they are wrongly offered.
- Slots on UTC day D+1 (a normal day for the organizer) match and are wrongly rejected as outside the override.

Separately, `dayjs(date.start).add(...).format(...)` formats in the server's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is in UTC. The comparison also breaks on any server not running in UTC.

The slot should be converted to `organizerTimeZone` and its local date compared with the override's date.

findings.title: Timezone-shifted overrides that cross invitee midnight are silently dropped
findings.body:
The shifted start/end are reduced to `hour()*60 + minute()`, which discards the day.

If shifting by `inviteeOffset - organizerOffset` pushes the override across the invitee's midnight, `endTime` wraps below `startTime`. Example: a UTC override 16:00–22:00 for an IST invitee becomes 21:30 → 1290 and 03:30 → 210.

`buildSlots` skips any boundary with `start >= end`, so the whole override vanishes. The user's working hours for that day have already been removed, so the invitee sees no slots at all from that host. The range needs to be split at midnight, or clamped to the invitee's day.

findings.title: Active-override day selection still uses the naive organizer wall time, so the new offset is applied to the wrong invitee day
findings.body:
`override.start` holds the organizer's wall-clock time stored as UTC. The filter `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, ...)` compares that naive value with real instants of the invitee's day, without converting it.

Example: an IST override on D 15:00–18:00 (real D 09:30Z = 19:30 Brisbane on D). For a Brisbane (+10) invitee the naive D T15:00Z falls in invitee day D+1.
- The shifted 19:30–22:30 window is shown on D+1.
- The host's normal working hours are removed on D+1.
- Day D keeps the normal working hours.

The PR's timezone fix is incomplete without converting `override.start` to a real instant, using `override.timeZone`, before this day filter.

findings.title: Missing override timeZone silently falls back to the server's local timezone
findings.body:
`TimeRange.timeZone` is optional. When it is undefined, `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` resolves to the process's local zone rather than UTC.

Any caller of `getSlots` that passes overrides without `timeZone` now gets them shifted by `inviteeOffset - serverLocalOffset`. Previously they were used as-is, so results now depend on the server or client machine timezone. Either require `timeZone` or skip the shift when it is absent.
